To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

purposive selection of sites from a gross arterial lesion for microscopic evaluation increases the probability of obtaining the required microscopic tissue characteristics in a low number of samples and that the increase is not as great as that which would have resulted if the number of samples had been greater.

the probability of obtaining a desired number of tissue blocks from a gross lesion or from a gross lesion free area is higher when purposive sampling is used rather than random sampling, but purposive sampling reduces the statistical inference.
purposive selection is more efficient than random selection when a small number of sites is used but the efficiency is reduced when a large number of sites is selected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optimizing the selection of tissue sites for microscopic evaluation of grossly visible lesions.
developing a probability model for selecting tissue sites in a gross lesion for microscopic study in order to maximize the probability of obtaining the tissue characteristics of interest.
the development and evaluation of a probability model for estimating the number of sites to be used in obtaining tissue blocks for microscopic evaluation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model provides a basis for estimating the probability of obtaining the required tissue characteristics in a purposive selection of tissue sites from a gross arterial specimen, but it does not provide a basis for making a conclusive statement regarding the probability of obtaining these characteristics.

purposive selection is more efficient than random selection for the purpose of obtaining tissue blocks from a gross arterial specimen for microscopic study when the number of sites is small, and that purposive selection becomes less efficient as the number of selected sites increases.
purposive selection is more effective in obtaining desired tissue characteristics than is random selection when a low number (less than or equal to 4) of sites is utilized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
purposive selection of tissue blocks is more efficient than random selection, but the statistical inference is limited.

purposive selection of sites is a better choice when only a small number of tissue blocks are to be examined, but random selection of sites is the better choice when a large number of tissue blocks is desired for statistical inference.

purposive selection of sites in the aorta is more effective than random selection when the number of sites is relatively small, but that random selection becomes more effective than purposive selection as the number of selected sites increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the investigator can select the number of tissue sites and their location in an artery to obtain the desired tissue characteristics.
the probability model can be used to help investigators choose a sample size and location for tissue blocks in order to obtain tissue blocks with the desired characteristics.

the probability of obtaining a block with a gross lesion and/or a block without a gross lesion can be estimated using the proposed method and the investigator can then choose the number and location of the sites to obtain the desired probability.
